title: Petite Square Huggies
category: Earrings (hinged soft-square hoops with 4 tiny pearls each, sold as 1 pair)
metal: 18k gold tone (listing: PVD 18K gold coating; base metal not stated), high mirror polish, warm saturated yellow; no brushing, no texture. The only other colour is the bright white of the pearls.
lock: 1 pair, 0 stones. Each hoop: 1 chunky tube bent into a 15 mm square, 4 softly rounded corners, round opening inside; 1 thin snap wire across the top; 1 hinge seam on the bottom bar; 4 white 1.5 mm pearls on the outer side walls, 2 per side. Mirror-polished 18k gold tone. Must stay 4 pinhead pearls on the side walls, never more, bigger or on the front face.
morph: The pearls. There are exactly 4 per hoop, each about 1.5 mm, set in tiny cups on the OUTER side walls of the two legs, 2 per leg, near the top and bottom corners (about 30% and 70% of the way down). Front-on they only peek out at the left and right edges; in profile they sit in a row of 2 along the leg. Image models add a 5th or 6th pearl, move pearls onto the front face or under the bottom bar, scatter them unevenly, or swell them into 2.5-4 mm beads. The listing's own earlier AI worn photos show it happening (edition-one/build/refs/square/listing-2.jpg: 5 pearls, some on the front face; listing-3.jpg: 3 visible, one under the bottom bar). Both were taken off the listing, and the current worn photo 03 still draws them about 2.5 mm. The old Edition One lock said 'a few seed pearls about 2.5mm', which invited this. Second risk is scale. Every earlier generation ran large: the E1 barfi hero measured about 23 mm (1.55x, edition-one/build/verify/heroes_b.json), colour ad r32a on a gift-box lid about 1.5x, and soan papdi 32b about 1.4x. Third is the shape. Models round it into an ordinary round hoop, sharpen it into a hard-cornered box or picture frame, or close the top with a thick 4th side. Any of these loses the thin snap wire and the round opening inside. Square outside, round inside is the signature.
sizeMm: 15 mm across, give or take 1 mm. Source: the listing's size guide (photo 05, also embedded in the description), which reads 'Huggie 15 mm across'; size-cards/cards.json agrees. Measured on 05 against its own 15 mm bar (252 px, 16.8 px/mm): the metal outline is about 14.7 mm wide and about 16 mm tall (the camera is slightly above, so a little of the top shows), and about 17.6 mm across the pearls. Pearls about 1.5 mm. The face of the tube is about 2-2.5 mm wide. The side wall is about 3.5 mm deep; that figure is an estimate from 01 and 02, against the pearl. The inner opening is a rounded oval about 10-11 mm wide. The snap wire is well under 1 mm. Referents: a little smaller than a 1-rupee coin (20 mm); about a fingernail wide (the E1 referent); half a 3 cm barfi square. Worn, it should span about a quarter of the ear's height (ear about 58 mm) and sit snug under the lobe. Worn photo 03 draws the hoop at about 0.42 of the ear's height, about 24 mm or 1.5x true size, so never use it for scale.

story: A hoop with corners: square outside, round inside. From across the room it reads geometric; up close it is soft and puffy, a mirror-polished tube with pillowy rounded corners. 4 pinhead pearls sit on the side walls, so front-on they peek out at the edges like tiny moons, and in profile 2 line up along the lobe like rivets. It is neat and 15 mm, sits close to the lobe, and is 'modern without being loud' (listing). Rs 899 against Rs 1,289 compare-at, on pre-order. The listing's styling tip is to stack it with a round hoop in the next piercing so the shapes play off each other: round for every day, square for the days you feel like it. Rhymes, best first. (1) CHAAR CHAAND: the Hindi idiom 'chaar chaand lagana', to add four moons, means to add glory, and this piece literally carries 4 small white moons. (2) CRICKET: a 'square cut' that goes for a 'chauka' (four), with chaukor = square, chauka = four and 4 pearls; 'Square cut. Four.' (3) SQUARING THE CIRCLE: the impossible geometry problem, solved in 15 mm, since the outside is square and the opening is round. (4) A LUDO DIE showing 4: the front view puts 4 pearls near the 4 corners. (5) CARROM: a square board, round pockets and white coins; the hoop sits in a corner pocket, or the pearls are the white carrom men. (6) A ship's PORTHOLE: a square plate, a round window and rivets. (7) The rounded-square family: an app icon, a keyboard keycap, a Polaroid frame, an old rounded-corner Doordarshan-era TV, a jharokha window. (8) Golden squares to eat: Mysore pak (a gold block with rounded edges), barfi, soan papdi; and the ice tray. Earlier ads, learned the hard way: the E1 ice-cube tray 'Cool, squared.' scored 9/10 in review (a shape rhyme, the one gold cell in a tray of ice). The barfi 'A square meal.' ran 1.55x. The gift box 'A square deal.' scored 8.9 but read 1.5x on a 7 cm lid. The soan papdi 'Too good to re-gift.' scored 9.1 but was dropped: the flaky threads look messy, a pistachio fleck crept in, and the hoops drew 1.4x. Give every prop a stated size and make the hoop a fraction of it (half a 3 cm barfi, three quarters of a 1-rupee coin). For video, the hinged snap clicks shut (an ASMR close-up). A slow turn takes it from front-on (corners, pearls at the edges) to profile (2 pearls in a row): a reveal shot.
copyNotes: Use: a hoop with corners, square with softly rounded corners, square outside and round inside, squared off, four tiny white pearls (two on each side), mirror polish, polished, catches the light on every corner, 18k gold tone, PVD 18k gold coating (a material fact only, never a durability promise), hinged snap, clicks shut, close to the lobe, small and neat, modern without being loud, 15 mm across, 1 pair, stack it with a round hoop, pre-order, Rs 899 (compare-at Rs 1,289). Hinglish that fits: chaar chaand, chaukor, chauka. Avoid: 'huggie'/'huggies' in body copy (an Indian nappy brand; the product title is the only exception), and baby or nappy-adjacent props such as a shape-sorter toy or blocks, which would amplify it. Never write 'gold', '18k gold', 'solid gold' or 'yellow gold' without 'tone'; the listing alt texts say 'yellow gold huggie', so never repeat them. Avoid 'anti-tarnish', 'tarnish free', 'waterproof', 'sweat-proof', 'stands up to sweat', 'keeps its colour' and 'hypoallergenic' (no claim tags), and water or wash rhymes that imply them (shower, swim, washing-machine). Avoid 'freshwater', 'cultured', 'real', 'natural' or 'Basra' pearl and 'mother of pearl'; the listing says only 'tiny round white pearls'. Avoid 'seed pearls about 2.5 mm' and 'a few pearls' (stale E1 lock; it is always 4 per hoop, about 1.5 mm), and any stone word (CZ, crystal, diamond). Avoid 'box', 'sharp corners', 'rectangle', 'cube' or 'frame' for the piece itself (it is a soft square with a round opening), and 'chunky statement', 'large', 'dangling' or 'drop'. Avoid 'silver', 'stainless steel' or any base metal (not listed). Avoid stale prices Rs 1,599 (Edition One) and Rs 999 (October colour ads), and 'fair and square' (in India 'fair' echoes skin-fairness). No ship-today or in-stock promises: it is pre-order.

It fills the frame, so it reads huge: no scale. Shopify alt says 'yellow gold huggie' (fix to 18k gold tone). Currently the listing's FEATURED image.
